title: Fishbone Diagram — Cart Abandonment
description: Drag ten candidate causes of cart abandonment onto the People, Process, Technology or Cost bone they belong to.
creator: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Systems Thinking in the Age of AI
Mental Models and Systems Analysis Tools
chapter_title: Mental Models and Systems Analysis Tools

educational.learningObjective: Given a list of candidate causes for a problem, the learner will categorize each cause onto the correct bone of a fishbone diagram.
prerequisites: Has seen a problem with more than one plausible cause
Knows that causes can be grouped by type
learningOutcomes: Categorize causes by type rather than by how obvious they are
Explain why some causes legitimately straddle two categories
Read a crowded bone as a finding about where to investigate
educational.assessmentOpportunity: Give learners three new candidate causes and ask which bone each belongs on, with a one-sentence justification. The justification matters more than the placement.

pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Retrieval practice with immediate right/wrong feedback and delayed explanation
pedagogical.feedbackType: Snap-and-checkmark on correct, shake-and-return on incorrect, plus an explanation on every placement
misconceptionsAddressed: That every cause belongs cleanly to exactly one category
That a fishbone is a list rather than an analysis
discussionQuestions: Which bone tends to get blamed first in your organization, and is that where the causes actually are?
What is lost when a cause could reasonably go on two bones and you have to pick one?
Why does the diagram deliberately include a cause the business cannot control?
